text: Access per graph: its owner, accounts with write access, and who may add notes
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: whoever creates a graph owns it. Write access can be granted to accounts. What guests may do is configured by the server admin or even per graph: making offers and making notes (like creating issues on GitHub). Creating a graph on a server needs that permission for the account.

No private graphs, decided by Felix 2026-11-12: limit complexity for now, and it is the "parency" in the name. Everyone may read every graph on a server.

Guests are accounts without rights on a graph, including automatic accounts.

Replaces the roles of today's hosted mode, which apply to the whole server (read, write, admin in access.ts). Rights are per graph, not per idea: the owner and accounts with write access may change everything in the graph, including committing in the UI.

Offers and notes themselves (the guest layer) are ideas b7e0b972 and 34b3d747.

Unchanged from 2026-11-10: write access never allows starting a terminal or an agent on the server.

Assumed by Claude, not said by Felix: the server admin sets the defaults and the owner of a graph may change them for that graph.

status.comment: Built 2026-11-13 (b2b6fd2a, 9102def6). Rights are per graph: owner, accounts with write access, everyone reads; the owner sets writers and who may leave notes (every account, selected accounts, nobody; server.json guestDefaults is the default) in the graph's settings or with `pnpm graphs`. Server-wide only: server admin, and whether an account may create graphs (server.json graphCreation). Write access never reaches agents, loops or server paths. Evidence: auth/auth.test.ts (owner, writer, stranger, visitor, server admin on one graph; paths refused; one graph's events only), guest/notes.test.ts (the owner's notes setting).
